statement: In a given circle to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular pentagon.
heath_proof: Let ABCDE be the given circle; thus it is required to inscribe in the circle ABCDE an equilateral and equiangular pentagon. Let the isosceles triangle FGH be set out having each of the angles at G, H double of the angle at F; [IV. 10] let there be inscribed in the circle ABCDE the triangle ACD equiangular with the triangle FGH, so that the angle CAD is equal to the angle at F and the angles at G, H respectively equal to the angles ACD, CDA; [IV. 2] therefore each of the angles ACD, CDA is also double of the angle CAD. Now let the angles ACD, CDA be bisected respectively by the straight lines CE, DB [I. 9], and let AB, BC, DE, EA be joined. Then, since each of the angles ACD, CDA is double of the angle CAD, and they have been bisected by the straight lines CE, DB, therefore the five angles DAC, ACE, ECD, CDB, BDA are equal to one another. But equal angles stand on equal circumferences; [III. 26] therefore the five circumferences AB, BC, CD, DE, EA are equal to one another. But equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines; [III. 29] therefore the five straight lines AB, BC, CD, DE, EA are equal to one another; therefore the pentagon ABCDE is equilateral. I say next that it is also equiangular. For, since the circumference AB is equal to the circumference DE, let BCD be added to each; therefore the whole circumference ABCD is equal to the whole circumference EDCB. And the angle AED stands on the circumference ABCD, and the angle BAE on the circumference EDCB; therefore the angle BAE is also equal to the angle AED. [III. 27] For the same reason each of the angles ABC, BCD, CDE is also equal to each of the angles BAE, AED; therefore the pentagon ABCDE is equiangular. But it was also proved equilateral; therefore in the given circle an equilateral and equiangular pentagon has been inscribed.
ai_proof_text:
4.11
**Statement:** In a given circle to inscribe an equilateral and equiangular pentagon.

**Step 1.** Let ABCDE be the given circle. By Proposition 4.10, construct an isosceles triangle FGH having each of the angles at G and H double the remaining angle at F.

**Step 2.** By Proposition 4.2, inscribe in circle ABCDE a triangle ACD equiangular with triangle FGH, so that angle CAD equals angle F, angle ACD equals angle G, and angle ADC equals angle H. Thus each of angles ACD and ADC is double of angle CAD.

**Step 3.** By Proposition 1.9, bisect angle ACD by the straight line CE, and bisect angle ADC by the straight line DB.

**Step 4.** Since angles ACD and ADC are each double of angle CAD, and CE bisects angle ACD while DB bisects angle ADC, it follows that the five angles DAC, ACE, ECD, CDB, and BDA are equal to one another.

**Step 5.** By Proposition 1.32, the three angles of triangle ACD sum to two right angles. Since angle ACD equals angle ADC equals twice angle CAD, we have angle CAD plus twice angle CAD plus twice angle CAD equals two right angles, that is, five times angle CAD equals two right angles. Therefore each of the five equal angles DAC, ACE, ECD, CDB, BDA is one-fifth of two right angles.

**Step 6.** Since equal inscribed angles stand on equal arcs, by Proposition 3.26 the arcs on which these equal angles stand are equal. Now angle BDA is an inscribed angle in circle ABCDE standing on arc AB; angle DAC stands on arc CD; angle ACE stands on arc DE; angle ECD stands on arc EA (since the angle at C in triangle ACD subtended by arc EA on the far side); and angle CDB stands on arc BC. Therefore arcs AB, BC, CD, DE, and EA are all equal to one another.

**Step 7.** By Proposition 3.29, equal arcs are subtended by equal straight lines. Therefore AB, BC, CD, DE, and EA are all equal to one another, and pentagon ABCDE is equilateral.

**Step 8.** It remains to show the pentagon is equiangular. Since arc AB equals arc DE, by Common Notion 2 adding arc BCD to each gives arc ABCD equal to arc BCDE. By Proposition 3.27, the inscribed angle AED stands on arc ABCD and the inscribed angle BAE stands on arc BCDE. Since these arcs are equal, angle AED equals angle BAE. By the same reasoning, applying equal arc additions and Proposition 3.27 to each vertex in succession, each angle of the pentagon equals every other. Therefore pentagon ABCDE is equiangular.

**Step 9.** Therefore in the given circle ABCDE an equilateral and equiangular pentagon has been inscribed, which is what was required. The pentagon is inscribed in the circle in the sense of Definition 4.3, since each vertex lies on the circumference, and the sides are fitted into the circle in the sense of Definition 4.7.
